### LOW: External prefix\-cache volume option changes the T\-041 at\-rest threat model \(TTL purge, volume trust\)
[CHANGELOG\.md:5](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/b0cc527890ba08d0ad2090e716a20655343e3502/CHANGELOG.md#L5) · A-001, T-041

CHANGELOG\.md line 5 adds \`darkbloom cache set \-\-directory \.\.\.\`, which moves encrypted SSD prefix\-cache files to an operator\-chosen external volume, and pins the volume UUID\. T\-041 assumes a single on\-box root \(darkbloom/kv3\)\. It also assumes the 30\-minute sliding TTL, the opportunistic sweep and the disk budget bound how long DBK3 artifacts exist\. If the external disk is unmounted or replaced, the provider 'refuses \.\.\. without falling back', so the sweep cannot run\. Encrypted files then persist on a removable, portable device well past the TTL\. The HMAC\-named files also keep leaking file count, sizes and mtimes\. The KEK stays on the Mac, which limits content exposure; the KEK wipe remains the crypto purge\. The threat model does not cover this new at\-rest location, the TTL\-expiry gap for detached media, or the trust placed in the volume UUID and 'encryption required' check\. Update T\-041 and TB\-007 to cover external roots\. State that TTL and LRU purge need the volume mounted, and that the KEK wipe is the only purge for detached media\. Confirm the encryption check cannot be bypassed by a user\-controlled mount\.

Raised by: anthropic/claude\-sonnet\-5\.5

### LOW: T\-041 at\-rest window and purge claims do not cover relocatable or external cache volumes
[docs/architecture/security/encryption\.md:187](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/b0cc527890ba08d0ad2090e716a20655343e3502/docs/architecture/security/encryption.md#L187) · A-001, ADV-001, T-041

The new section documents \`darkbloom cache set \-\-directory\`, which can put DBK3 payloads on an external APFS volume\. It also admits that TTL/LRU deletion needs the volume mounted\. Detached or inaccessible media can keep ciphertext and metadata indefinitely, and switching locations leaves old ciphertext behind\. Restart freshness is seeded from mtimes, so a malicious disk can replay valid files and metadata\. A filesystem\-UUID pin can be defeated by cloning the UUID\. T\-041 and its mitigations still say the at\-rest window is bounded by a 30\-minute sliding TTL and a box\-wide LRU budget\. They name \`darkbloom/kv3\` as the only on\-disk root, and describe KEK wipe as the purge\. Nothing in them covers an operator\-chosen, possibly removable store\. A malicious operator or enclosure controller retains ciphertext plus visible size, time and model metadata past the TTL \(ADV\-001\)\. It can also replay still\-valid files\. Fix: update T\-041 to add the selectable volume as a new at\-rest surface with these residuals\. Reword the TTL and LRU mitigations as 'while mounted'\. Add the UUID\-pin limitation and make the KEK wipe the only guaranteed purge\. Add the cache\-volume files named in the PR to its detection\_hint and affected\_files\.

Raised by: anthropic/claude\-sonnet\-5\.5

### LOW: Removable\-disk cache option is not reflected in the threat model \(A\-001 / T\-041\)
[docs/provider/cache\-storage\.md:46](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/b0cc527890ba08d0ad2090e716a20655343e3502/docs/provider/cache-storage.md#L46) · A-001, T-041, TB-003

docs/provider/cache\-storage\.md documents a new operator\-selected external/separate volume for encrypted SSD prefix\-cache payloads, which are derived from consumer prompts \(A\-001\)\. The same page states that expiry cannot delete files on detached or previously selected disks, and that \`\-\-reset\-directory\` and re\-selecting a disk leave old files in place\. The result is a retention and exfiltration surface outside the internal disk\. It consists of detached media, a volume\-UUID pin, \`provider\.toml\` as a trust anchor, and the operator's choice of removable hardware with unverified firmware\. Visible threat\-model text does not cover this\. The T\-041 cache entry was too large to inspect here, so I could not confirm whether it already covers it\. The PR is docs\-only, so I could not verify in code that payloads stay HMAC\-keyed and encrypted with keys kept off the removable volume\. Fix: add a TB\-003/T\-041 entry for external cache volumes with their residual risks \(orphaned ciphertext, attacker\-swapped volumes, a tampered \`provider\.toml\` redirecting the cache, unlimited daily writes\)\. Confirm in the implementing PR that keys never reside on the cache volume\.

Raised by: anthropic/claude\-sonnet\-5\.5

### LOW: T\-041 needs updating for operator\-configurable SSD cache root and volume binding
[docs/reference/configuration\.md:896](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/b0cc527890ba08d0ad2090e716a20655343e3502/docs/reference/configuration.md#L896) · T-041

The patch documents \`cache\.directory\` and \`cache\.volume\_uuid\`, which move the encrypted SSD prefix\-cache payloads to an operator\-chosen absolute directory \(the \`darkbloom/kv3\` child\) on a possibly external or removable volume\. It also documents \`cache\.daily\_write\_gb\`, where \`0\` means an unlimited write budget\. T\-041 and its detection\_hint still describe a fixed on\-disk root \(\`darkbloom/kv3\`\) and a fixed\-posture disk policy\. That policy uses an available\-disk/2 budget, a 20 GiB pre\-write reserve and a 750 GB/day write cap\. The model does not cover the following changes in at\-rest exposure: \- Cache files can sit on a volume that can be detached or shared, or that has different permissions\. \- The volume\-UUID check happens only when the directory is opened, so it does not cover the cache path becoming unavailable later\. \- An unlimited write budget removes the SSD wear/DoS bound\. HMAC\-named, AES\-GCM encrypted files and the TTL still apply\. T\-041 should be updated to list the configured root and volume binding as part of the purge, TTL and disk\-budget surface, and to state whether the free\-space reserve and TTL sweep apply on the configured volume\.

Raised by: anthropic/claude\-sonnet\-5\.5
